beats: Maya moved from Winnipeg to Calgary for a new job and spent six thousand dollars. She can deduct all of it. Just not all this year.
The test: your new home must be at least forty kilometres closer to the new job. Winnipeg to Calgary passes easily.
What counts: the movers, the trip, and temporary lodging. Six thousand dollars in total.
The catch: the deduction only comes from income earned at the new job. She started in November and earned four thousand dollars there.
So she deducts four thousand this year, and carries the other two thousand forward to next year's pay from the same job.
Keep every receipt, and if your employer paid you back, don't claim that part.
